source_documents.title: Synthesis and photophysical properties of quaternaphthalenes: topology-dependent radiative dynamics in deep-blue emitters

reference_evidence_units.quote: Several QNps, especially 126151 and 126261, showed high fluorescence quantum yields and large radiative rate constants, whereas 126272 exhibited a smaller radiative rate and a longer fluorescence lifetime, indicating suppression of the radiative transition probability by a specific linkage topology.
reference_evidence_units.subject: QNps
reference_evidence_units.statement: Linkage topology sets the radiative rate constant.

reference_evidence_units.quote: TD-DFT calculations showed that highly emissive QNps possess large oscillator strengths and mainly HOMO–LUMObased S1 ← S0 transitions.
reference_evidence_units.subject: QNps
reference_evidence_units.statement: Bright isomers have large S1 oscillator strengths.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The negligible solvent dependence of the fluorescence spectra supports locally excited π–π* emissive states rather than intramolecular charge-transfer states.
reference_evidence_units.subject: QNps
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission is LE ππ*, not CT.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Topology-dependent oscillator strength and radiative rate govern the emission (high quantum yield from a large radiative rate constant).
